messages.subject: R-RApache to develop Knowledge Base
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I need your opinion about using R-Rapache to build a knowlegde base to bioinformatics field.

I have copious amount of genotype information (some few million records) and would like to store it in MySQL database. Then, using RMySQL connector I would like to use it for further analysis using R over a web interface. The web interface which I am thnking off, just does not serve the purose of statistical analysis, it should also serve as displaying data in grids and interactive maps etc on web interface.

I had thought of doing the same using python-MySQLdb to store data and then R-rpy for further statistical analysis. But as R is now directly made to work on web I am very much excited about RApache project. Very recently I was introducing Rapache project and concept of building knowledge base using Rapache-R-MySQL combination to our team memebrs, Unfortunately few memebers were not that happy with using R directly in middle tier. There were serious comments about R that it is slow and generating plots on the fly wont be too fast. there was also discussion about maturity of RMySQL database connector, i mean fastness of querying MySQL will vary significantly with RMySQL when campared to MySQLdb connector?

It would be nice if you give me a detailed opinion on this.

Thanking you all in anticipation.

Regards,
mlsc

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am not sure about your data structure, but if you do not alter those often from third-party programs, then storing the information in R's native file formats (like RData) might give you some performance boost against always querying MySQL. Of course this depends on data structure and volume. Also, checking out some NoSQL techniques (like CouchDB or redis) might be a good idea for a web service - if your data is not profiting from relational database structure. Well, you need some benchmarks here.
About plots: I would not say that the base graphics library (or even lattice) would be slow, although ggplot2 has some issues. So IMHO it depends on what type of plots would you generate, but I would say there would be no serious performance issues.
After all: I think going the direct R way is great option :)

Best,
Gergely

messages.subject_clean: RSQLite / rApache on a RHEL 5 system
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

My rApache script works well on a Debian 32bit system. Now I am trying
to move it to a RHEL5.6 64bit system. The system has been updated. The
R (2.14) was grabbed from EPEL, then rApache (1.1.16) and a few R
packages including RSQLite were installed. Everything works well,
except apache crashes once the code tries to connect a SQLite database
through RSQLite.  The error message is similar to Rajarshi's (http://
groups.google.com/group/rapache/browse_thread/thread/ <http://groups.google.com/group/rapache/browse_thread/thread/>
d93f304b642bbd73/1003a5fece3b6c90) (cannot post to that topic):

*** glibc detected *** /usr/sbin/httpd: free(): invalid pointer:
0x00002ab860fc0318 ***
======= Backtrace: =========
/lib64/libc.so.6[0x2ab8506a445f]
/lib64/libc.so.6(cfree+0x4b)[0x2ab8506a48bb]
/usr/lib64/R/library/RSQLite/libs/RSQLite.so(sqlite3_initialize+0x2b1)
[0x2ab86245d5b1]
/usr/lib64/R/library/RSQLite/libs/RSQLite.so[0x2ab862489a4d]
/usr/lib64/R/library/RSQLite/libs/RSQLite.so(RS_SQLite_newConnection
+0x11c)[0x2ab86244877c]
/usr/lib64/R/lib/libR.so[0x2ab85c0cd1d6]
/usr/lib64/R/lib/libR.so(Rf_eval+0x650)[0x2ab85c0fd650]
...

It is surprising that the same R code including SQLite database
connection and query part works in R shell, but not in rApache
environment. R shell and rApache should use the same RSQLite.so,
right? How can they behave differently?

I rebuilt the R from the source code, the rApache and R packages; also
updated the RHEL to 5.7.  The problem still cannot be solved.

I suspected the SQLite was too old (3.3.6), so I installed a local
version 3.7.10, then compiled the RSQLite again. Still the same. I
also built a CentOS 5.6 system which should be identical to RHEL 5.6,
and it does has the same SQLite 3.3.6. Amazingly the code works in
rApache on this CentOS 5.6!

So there must be some problems in my RHEL5 box.

Any clues? Many thanks!

Qiang

messages.subject_clean: "Sticky" brew-rapache files, possible URL routing issue
messages.body_plain:
I am seeing an issue with URL routing under rApache for pages that include brew code. Effectively rhtml pages are "sticky" until the apache server is restarted. No errors are generated in the logs. RApacheInfo runs correctly. The example below uses brew 1.0-6 rApache 1.1.16, prototype.js 1.7 running on Mac OSX 10.7.3 server containing Apache 2.2.21. My configuration follows a suggestion from the mailing list to configure Apache to recognize .rhtml extension as per Jeffrey Horner's post of Oct 4 2010, 1:31 pm your apache config: SetHandler r-script RHandler brew::brew Create three simple test files with source listed below at the bottom of this message: html file listing links: main.html two linked rhtml files: first_page.rhtml and second_page.html Each of the latter two files contains a simple pair of boxes for entering a couple of dates and a chart button which for purposes of this discussion can be considered a dummy action. Enable the web server. Go to the main.html file web server link: http:///tests/main.html Navigate to the First linked rhtml page. You should see the title: First page results. Go back to main.html Navigate to the Second linked rhtml page. You should see the title: Second page results, but what I see is a reload of the First linked page entitled First page results. Shutdown and restart the web server. Go to the main page and then navigate to the second link. Note the title. Return to the main page. Go to the first link. This time the second link's title sticks even when navigating to the first page, effectively the mirror behavior of the first case. Reseting the browser cache makes no difference. The problem is server side (multiple machines targetting the same URL produce the same result). Note also it is browser independent, since curl commands produce the same results. It leads to other complications in rendering brew pages including duplicate javascript insertions. Note that if main.html is instead named with an .rhtml extension but contains either no brew code, or a trivial snippet, the links do not work properly (the browser switches to the right URL, but the page is not accessible). If the "chart" javascript buttons are enabled the stickiness described here causes the previous page to be appended to the original page, but I believe that if I can fix the problem described here, that issue should be more easily isolated. Is this a URL routing problem inside rApache? 		DefaultType text/html
	</Directory>

think you know this...)

the others tell apache how to deal with files in folder '....../brew'.

after you add this and restart your server, you could put a test file
'test.brew' in the folder above, with these content:

<%
x<-1:10
print(x)
%>
